analysis: The closest option combines single and multivariable calculus, linear algebra, numerical methods, probability, proof and discrete structures with algorithms, linear systems, vision, optimisation, decision theory and robotics. Databases and operating systems contribute the environment for computation. Ethics and philosophy contextualise practice and argument without substituting for pure mathematics. Discrete proof is substantive but introductory.

The statistical option shares the quantitative core and replaces five technology-focused courses with research methods, empirical brain and behaviour preparation, software development, econometrics and meta-analysis. Econometrics adds estimation and model checks with Monte Carlo simulation; advanced research methods develops systematic review and evidence synthesis. Its empirical and methodological organising focus materially differs from vision, robotics, optimisation and reinforcement learning.

The UCR workbook supports calculus, introductory proofs, vector spaces and numerical analysis, with no cumulative proof-based sequence through analysis, topology, geometry, group theory or abstract algebra. The closest option supplies some cryptography foundations through discrete structures and algorithms without specialist cryptography coursework. No third option has sufficient disciplinary substance. Both options pass actual offering, credit and prerequisite checks.

alignment.rationale: Both develop statistical modelling; UCR applies multivariate models in behavioural research rather than mathematical statistics.
Both develop programming for problem-solving; UCR teaches general Python rather than a mathematics-specific scientific-programming course.
Both use logic, sets and proof. Groningen extends this foundation into a sustained analysis and algebra sequence.
Both introduce differentiation and integration. UCR also uses complex numbers and differential equations in a dynamic modelling project.
Both directly study systems, vectors, matrices and linear spaces; Groningen continues to a second dedicated course.
Both establish probability distributions; UCR combines probability with statistical inference and simulation.
Both use interpolation, integration and equation-solving algorithms. UCR tests accuracy and stability with Mathematica, while Groningen uses Python.
Both use differential equations and feedback to study linear systems. UCR emphasises signal processing and transforms. Groningen includes controllability and state observation.
Both extend calculus; UCR includes multivariable and complex-valued functions but not the target analysis sequence.
